name: Infectious, Fungal or Parasitic Myopathy

criteria.description: Muscle biopsy showing fungal or parasitic organisms with associated inflammatory infiltrate
Identification of fungal or parasitic pathogen by culture, PCR, or serology
Subacute or chronic proximal muscle weakness with myalgia and elevated muscle enzymes
MRI showing muscle edema and inflammation consistent with infectious myopathy
Clinical improvement following targeted antifungal or antiparasitic treatment

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical presentation plus microbiological confirmation and histopathological evidence
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of autoimmune and other non-infectious myopathies.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Muscle biopsy demonstrating fungal or parasitic organisms
searchTerms: muscle biopsy showing fungal or parasite infection
fungal or parasitic organisms in muscle
proximal muscle weakness developing over weeks

common.symptomName: Myalgia localized to affected muscle groups
Swelling or edema of affected muscles

occasional.symptomName: Cutaneous lesions or skin rash associated with fungal infection
Weight loss due to chronic infection
searchTerms: unintentional weight loss due to illness

occasional.symptomName: Dysphagia from involvement of oropharyngeal muscles
searchTerms: difficulty swallowing from throat muscle involvement
trouble eating due to muscle weakness

occasional.symptomName: Respiratory symptoms secondary to systemic fungal dissemination
searchTerms: lung problems from systemic fungal infection
respiratory issues due to fungal dissemination

rare.symptomName: Cardiac arrhythmias due to myocardial involvement
Ocular involvement with uveitis or retinitis
searchTerms: eye inflammation affecting retina or uvea

rare.symptomName: Neuropathic pain from peripheral nerve involvement
searchTerms: nerve pain from peripheral nerve damage
burning or shooting pain in limbs

laboratory: Elevated serum creatine kinase (CK) and inflammatory markers
Positive fungal or parasitic serology or PCR
Muscle biopsy with granulomatous inflammation and pathogen identification
imaging: MRI showing muscle edema and inflammation
other: Response to antifungal or antiparasitic therapy
Exclusion of autoimmune myopathies by autoantibody testing

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of infectious organisms on biopsy
Response to immunosuppressive therapy rather than antimicrobials
History of exposure to myotoxic drugs or toxins
Lack of infectious agents in muscle biopsy
Improvement after withdrawal of offending agent

redFlags: Rapidly progressive muscle weakness with systemic signs of infection
Failure to respond to standard immunosuppressive therapy
Evidence of disseminated fungal or parasitic infection
references: Dalakas MC. Inflammatory muscle diseases. N Engl J Med. 2015;372(18):1734-1747.
Dalakas MC. Infectious myopathies. Neurol Clin. 2014;32(3):717-735.
